utterances.text: Mr. Mole, in the course of the examination-in-chief yesterday, when asked by my learned colleague a question regarding the obtaining of a rank of General Galic, that is, his promotion, I will paraphrase what you said. I believe that was page 45 of the transcript. According to you, that he also got his promotion because of his success in his work but that this didn't mean that it was necessarily linked to Sarajevo. Did I interpret correctly what you said?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a fair interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you know which rank should a corps commander hold, according to the rules of the army of Republika Srpska or generally, according to any army rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there is any ability for me to make a general rule about such an appointment. I can only relate it to my own personal experience. And a corps commander would expect to be a major-general in the British Military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, I can tell you that according to the rules of the army of Republika Srpska, this rank --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, there is an objection against -- perhaps I would first give the opportunity to Mr. Ierace. Perhaps you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would finish what your question would be because there was no question yet. You were just informing us about something. And then see whether the objection still stands. What would be your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, would you agree with me that Mr. Galic, as a -- in a rank of a colonel, he was appointed in a formational post, which both at peace and in war would actually be holding the rank of a general?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no further objections, so please answer the question, Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said before, I don't believe that pure rank necessarily indicates the size of unit that an individual commands. Each circumstance is different. And the experience of the former Republic of Yugoslavia, where their military was broken into many pieces, would indicate that normal accepted ranks, as they relate to unit size, would similarly be distorted.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, could you tell us, during your mandate, did you have reports that from the area of Butmir, which was under the control of the BH army, there was shelling in the direction of the airport? Did you have such reports?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking whether Butmir was the source of rounds landing in the airport, then the answer is yes. Do I understand the question correctly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Mole. Yesterday, you told us that the front line in Sarajevo, according to you, was the length of 64 kilometres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, do you think that a corps commander could have known at any point in time what was happening on such a long line of front?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He might not know the detail but he would certainly be expected to comprehend such issues as logistic resupply. And if I may take as an example, units were using ammunition, it would be a fair question to ask those unit commanders why they were using that ammunition. Whether he was present or not, it is his job to know what his commanders are doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, in your opinion, did the Serb forces have such communication equipment, communication means, that they were able to have -- to be constantly aware of the situation at any location on the front line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had such communications, although not ideal, that allowed them the policy of containment which I have already outlined to you. The fact that they could fulfil that role indicates that their command and control was sufficient for their purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, was this on every single point on the front line? Was this so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have indicated that it would be difficult as relates to certain locations but there was plenty of time, even during my tenure, for improvements to be made to permit communications which were sufficient for their purpose. If they had not achieved that level of communication, then if I was the commander, I would be discussing it very carefully with my communication commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my co-counsel will continue the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were three months in Sarajevo. Would you agree with me to consider that this was a period which is relatively short?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Same question: A relatively short period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question serves no purpose at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's an objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is that it serves no purpose at all. Can you please indicate what would enlighten the Chamber whether the witness considers the period of four months, which is approximately 120 days, to be relatively long or relatively short.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Because I am going along the line of questions that I have. But I will discover that -- I intend to ask the witness a long line of questions regarding the locations he may have visited in Sarajevo going by location and location. And that is the reason I am asking the witness whether four months have seemed to him a sufficient amount of time to do a -- to make a tour of all the locations that we are interested in in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's assume that it would assist. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, would you agree with me, sir, to consider that a period of four months is a relatively short period of time to see everything that is going on in a city like Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not particularly. The period depends upon intensity of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So, sir, since you answer in the negative, and only in order to gain time, I am going to ask you certain questions as a list. If you know one of the names from this list of people or locations, please stop me. If not, we will assume that you don't know them. So the question is the following: Do you know, as an example, the names, the following names: Stela, Kulin Ban, Benevolencija, Kobra, Sultan Fatih. So far you have no knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ljiljana; Zulfikar; Crni Labudovi, Black Swans; Akrepi, Silver Fox; Mudris; Dedo? Sir, you don't know any of these locations -- any of these names, do you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So let us continue: Silos. Still, you don't know it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Borsalino, Tarcin, Kazani? Do you know these names?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pavle Goranin; sir, do you know this name?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gras, Petar Dakic; Do you know these names?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew a Dakic, but the screen hasn't come up with the spelling. It has now. But whether it was the same one, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think this is not a name of a person but a name of a location. Did you know of a location called Petar Dakic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I knew an individual called Dakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Sir, all of these names, they don't ring any bells for you, do they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, you cannot tell us if the names of Zulfikar, Crni Labudovi, Akrepi, Mudris, Dedo, would correspond to special units that were located or positioned on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you don't know if on this mount, Mount Igman, there was also a Mujahedin unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew the heavy weapons which were located on that mount only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to that later. Sir, do you recall the name of MUP? Does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am going to ask you -- I will ask you some questions later in relation to all of these names. We will come back to that later. But before that, I would like to ask you one question: Do you know where was located in relation to what is sometimes known as the Egyptian Battalion, the 10th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking what the relative positions between the Egyptian Battalion and the 10th Mountain Brigade were?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am saying I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Witness, I understand that it has been long time, but a town map cannot simply evaporate from one's mind. Do you have any idea of where this was, at one end of the city or the other end of the city? Or were perhaps these two locations next to each other, close to each other?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I understand your question to be at variance to my first understanding. You said what the relative positions between the Egyptian Battalion and the 10th Mountain Brigade. If you are now asking me, do I recall where the Egyptian Battalion was, then the answer to the question is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know where the 10th Brigade was located with respect to the Egyptian Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I can't recall the detail from the operational map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. May I now ask you to go back to what I mentioned a moment ago. We are speaking in broad terms. Was it located far from the Egyptian Battalion, relatively close to them, near them? Can you approximate how far was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have just told you I don't know the relative positions between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we, therefore, conclude that your memory in respect of these events today needs a lot of refreshing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking me specific questions as relate to many individuals who I did meet and the relative positions of the two sides, it was never the UN's purpose to plot and understand every single commander. I think, sir, you have forgotten, we had 60 UN military observers. That does not permit us to know every commander on every side. And because I do not recall those commanders because I would only deal with a number does not negate my very clear memory of the events during my tenure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But I can then take note of the fact that your memory is quite clear, but that you cannot simply remember the distance between these two points. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which two points?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A and B, that is, the Egyptian Battalion and the 10th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you take that specific example, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to ask you a question concerning other points in town, but can I expect the same kind of answer; if I ask you about the 5th Brigade and the closest observation point, would your answer be roughly the same?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had hoped from what I have already told you that you would understand that the mandate which I had did not, and I say again, did not relate to military intelligence, which is the sort of question that you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. Thank you very much, Witness. So I conclude that, generally speaking, you did not have precise information on various locations of the points that I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I also conclude from your previous response, that is, can I interpret it as follows: You had a relatively small number of observers to monitor all this; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, for the same reason as my earlier objection, that is, inviting the witness to observe whether his numbers were relatively small or otherwise is of no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My recollection is that it was 64. Are we talking about the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not 64. 64 is the number of the kilometres of the front line. I think that the witness mentioned the figure of 60 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I give the same response as we did before, that is, that the Chamber is wondering whether the assessment of whether 60 is relatively much -- or is a relatively high number or low number might not that much assist. On the other hand, Mr. Ierace, objecting against it is not of great assistance either, we think. So, therefore, if you want to spend time to cross-examination to this, perhaps -- please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that according to you - at least that is how I understand your testimony - approximately 60 monitors was a relatively small number for the task that you had been entrusted with; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was quite a small number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me move to another issue. Following the Prosecution in their phrasing of the questions, we have testimony to the effect that the majority -- most of the destruction of civilian property, including residence buildings, was located on or in the vicinity of the front line, that is, outside of what was going on in the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if that question refers to testimony by other witnesses, then it is entirely inappropriate because it could not be said that the Defence has any understanding that that is common ground with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that, Mr. President. If I may rephrase, I am following the Prosecution because on several occasions, the Prosecution said, in order to spare time, I submit to you what other testimonies are. I am doing exactly the same Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. thing that Mr. Ierace was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... such information. So if you would asked: "Would it be correct to say that," then give the same content, then you do not refer to any testimony given in this court. I think that is the main source of the objection, not that you confront the witness with what is contained in the testimony, what is the evidence in such testimony, but that you relate it to testimony in this court. Well, since you have done it already, please keep this in mind for the next questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just to save time, I don't have any objection to the Defence putting questions in that form where it is understood clearly that the material is common ground between the parties. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. But since this is not, then no reference to other testimony and, of course, if you would say that there is testimony that Sarajevo was located next to the river Miljacka, then of course it would -- so that is a restriction on what I just told you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that in Sarajevo, during your tenure, most of the destruction caused by the property happened at the front line or around the front line; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And why, briefly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why what? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what reason? What is the reason of your response, why do you say no? Can you please explain.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because much of the destruction of the city occurred across the city, the opposite to what you said, hence, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Are you telling us that there was more damage in the centre of the town than at the front line? I am referring to the front lines in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is extremely difficult to quantify damage. If you are talking about any particular part of the city being more likely to be damaged than any other, in my experience, the front line was set when I arrived. Much damage there had already been done. And during my tenure there, an awful lot more damage occurred away from the front lines in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I take note of that. Witness, do you know, yes or no, please, if the Serbs at one point in time or another wanted a demilitarisation of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware through the workings of the mixed military working group that both sides would appreciate that situation. That is not a "yes" or "no" because I can't provide yes or no to complicated questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am doing my best, but I don't think it will be possible to shorten your testimony because we again spend some time on technical issues and that is the reason why I wanted you to reply with yes or no. So in the interest of speed. Thank you very much. Let me continue. Have you ever heard again, yes or no, of an operation called "Oxygen"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true Witness, that your forces didn't keep any record of the number of the wounded and the casualties during your mandate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not one of the functions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true, Witness, that there were two major hospitals in Sarajevo, the State Hospital and the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it further correct that these hospitals were more or less the same, in terms of size? In terms of capacity.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to go back to the issue of mobile targets. Do you know if there was a possibility for the Sarajevo forces, that is, the government forces as they were referred to, to use civilian vehicles for the purposes of transport of light mortars; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you personally see any such vehicles and if so, which one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Soft-skinned vehicles, of normal commercial type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us more precisely, for instance, whether any Golf cars or any other types?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many types, but my understanding was the Volkswagen depot adjacent to Sarajevo had had a number of vehicles removed from it during the conflict and were used for Presidency transportation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean as the vehicles used by the army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The vehicles used by the army, were they distinctive in any way? Could they be distinguished from other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had no specific markings that indicated that they were military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But these vehicles, were they used for military or logistic operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there any other types of vehicles apart from Golf?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were other civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As many variable vehicles as you would expect to find in any city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Witness, that the fuel market was under the control of the army?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You refer to the Presidency army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, of the Presidency forces, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have been foolish not to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So it would be foolish of me to continue with questions in this line at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I think that we can continue tomorrow with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...in keeping in mind that only a couple of minutes will be taken by the Defence, how much time you would need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me confer with the General. When I said a few minutes, this was translated with a couple of minutes. But actually, what I meant to say was a few couples of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that the couple of minutes in English means some minutes and not a couple to be understood as two minutes. We will adjourn in one minute but, Mr. Ierace, after we concluded the testimony of this witness, would that be a suitable moment to discuss a few procedural issues tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we will start, depending on how many questions the Judges would have, at approximately 9.30 tomorrow, discussing procedural issues and, Mr. Mole, would you please return tomorrow morning for a short period of time to this courtroom. We will adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You caught me already today. So when I make a mistake once. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what else would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am truly sorry, Mr. President, but in accordance to your usual rule, we would need a couple seconds extra, I am trying not to inconvenience. If I do it tomorrow, I think it would be post facto. Thank you very much. 25.25. Each time I am talking about the page and the line. "Many" was used by the witness and cannot be translated as "beaucoup d'hommes," because we also know there were women there. 26.25, another correction to be made. 27.3. "Position of their army" is not the same as "disposition of the army." The same goes for page 11. Another problem in interpretation concerning the word "checkpoint." 46.20. A large portion has not -- was not correctly interpreted, talking about the rank of the General. I don't think that the General was appointed to the "poste de formation," as it has been interpreted in French. Thank you very much for your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
